input.fullContext:
You are in a benchmark workspace containing a Rust reference application at ./rust-reference and an official reference CLI path recorded in ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt.

Goal:
Create a Python implementation that is a 1:1 functional port of the reference application for this benchmark. For the same input, the official reference CLI and your rebuilt version must produce exactly the same observable result: exit status, stdout, and stderr.

Reference:
- Project: eza
- Source language: Rust
- Target language: Python
- Repository: https://github.com/eza-community/eza.git
- Release/tag: v0.23.3
- Commit: 05d20d11c488b2ad3f0d63ac0b529281cc1c16ef
- Local source copy: ./rust-reference
- Official reference CLI: read ./REFERENCE_BINARY.txt
- Behavior area: directory listing, long view, tree, sort, hidden, icons/colors disabled

Hard constraints:
- Do not use Docker.
- Do not search the internet.
- Do not look for, copy, adapt, vendor, install, or import an existing Python implementation, clone, wrapper, compatibility layer, or package for this application.
- Use ./rust-reference and the official reference CLI as the only functional sources of truth.
- Implement in Python.
- Do not shell out to the official reference CLI from your implementation.
- Do not install packages that already implement this application or its command suite.
- The root deliverable must include ./compile.sh.
- ./compile.sh must build or wrap your Python implementation and leave a runnable root command named ./executable. On Windows, ./executable.exe or ./executable.cmd is also accepted.
- The first entrypoint discovered by the evaluator must itself be directly runnable on the current OS/runtime; do not leave a higher-priority wrapper, placeholder, or script that requires a different interpreter than the evaluator will use.
- The harness will run ./compile.sh and then invoke your runnable executable with the same argv used for the official reference CLI.

Deliverable shape:
- Keep the actual implementation in one or more Python files, for example ./main.py or ./eza_port.py.
- ./compile.sh must be idempotent and must create only entrypoints that are directly runnable by the evaluator on this machine.
- The evaluator checks entrypoints in this order: ./executable, ./executable.exe, ./executable.cmd, ./executable.bat, ./executable.js, ./executable.py, ./executable.jar.
- For a Python target, if ./executable exists, it must be valid Python source that can be run as: python ./executable <args>. Do not make ./executable a POSIX shell script.
- On Windows, prefer creating ./executable.cmd that calls your Python file. If you create ./executable.cmd, remove any POSIX shell wrapper named ./executable so it cannot be discovered first.
- On Unix-like systems, either make ./executable valid Python source with a Python shebang or make sure the current evaluator will not run it through the wrong interpreter.
- Do not leave stale, broken, placeholder, or higher-priority entrypoints in the workspace after ./compile.sh runs.

Equivalence requirements:
- For every evaluated invocation, running the official reference CLI and running your rebuilt executable with the same argv, stdin, files, and environment must produce the same exit status, stdout, and stderr.
- If the official binary prints nothing, your program must print nothing.
- If the official binary writes to stderr, your program must write to stderr.

Do not ask the user questions. Infer from source and official CLI behavior.

+# Python eza port architecture
+
+## Compatibility boundary
+
+The rebuilt command is compatible only when its process result matches the
+official v0.23.3 Windows binary byte-for-byte: exit status, stdout, and stderr.
+The Rust source under `rust-reference/` defines behavior; the executable named
+by `REFERENCE_BINARY.txt` is the observable oracle.
+
+The benchmark scope is directory listing, long view, tree traversal, sorting,
+hidden-file filtering, and operation with icons and colors disabled. Parser and
+runtime errors in those paths remain part of the contract.
+
+## Modules
+
+- `eza_port.py`: process entry point and exit-code boundary.
+- `eza_py/options.py`: eza-compatible short/long option parser and option
+  deduction. Later occurrences override earlier occurrences, matching the Rust
+  `MatchedFlags` behavior.
+- `eza_py/filesystem.py`: filesystem entries, Windows attributes, filtering,
+  natural sorting, directory expansion, and recursion.
+- `eza_py/render.py`: line, grid, long-table, and tree renderers. Renderers
+  consume modeled entries and never invoke the reference binary.
+- `.tura/script/differential.py`: backward-compatibility verifier. It creates
+  controlled fixtures, runs the oracle and candidate independently, and
+  compares all three process observables as bytes.
+
+## Stable behavior derived from the source
+
+- Option errors use status 3 (`rust-reference/src/main.rs:141`); missing input
+  paths are reported while processing continues and produce status 2
+  (`rust-reference/src/main.rs:272`).
+- Redirected output defaults to one entry per line; a set width or `--grid`
+  selects grid output (`rust-reference/src/options/view.rs:43`).
+- On Windows, leading-dot and leading-underscore entries are hidden unless
+  `--all`/`--almost-all` is active (`rust-reference/src/fs/dir.rs:166`).
+- Sorting is stable, natural, case-insensitive by default, then optionally
+  reversed and grouped by directory (`rust-reference/src/fs/filter.rs:136`).
+- Tree rows are depth-first and use `├──`, `│`, and `└──` trunk state
+  (`rust-reference/src/output/tree.rs:77`).
+- Windows long mode renders mode, size, and selected timestamps but not Unix
+  owner/group/inode/link fields (`rust-reference/src/output/table.rs:75`).
+
+## Entrypoint contract
+
+`compile.sh` is idempotent. On Windows it removes higher-priority extensionless
+entrypoints and emits `executable.cmd`; on Unix-like systems it emits a valid,
+executable Python launcher named `executable`. It does not compile, download,
+or vendor another implementation.
+
+## Validation gates
+
+1. Python syntax compilation for every implementation and verifier module.
+2. Idempotent `compile.sh` execution and direct entrypoint smoke test.
+3. Focused parser and renderer unit tests.
+4. Full `.tura/script/differential.py` corpus against the official binary,
+   comparing status and raw stdout/stderr.
+5. Independent end-to-end invocation through the generated root entrypoint.
+
+No passing gate is accepted as a proxy for another gate; the differential
+corpus must explicitly cover each benchmark behavior area.
*** End Patch

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Byte-exact compatibility checks for the local eza Python port."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+REFERENCE = Path((ROOT / "REFERENCE_BINARY.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Case:
+    name: str
+    args: tuple[str, ...]
+    stdin: bytes | None = None
+    env: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Result:
+    status: int
+    stdout: bytes
+    stderr: bytes
+
+
+def run(command: list[str], case: Case, cwd: Path) -> Result:
+    env = os.environ.copy()
+    env.update(case.env)
+    completed = subprocess.run(
+        [*command, *case.args],
+        cwd=cwd,
+        env=env,
+        input=case.stdin,
+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+        check=False,
+    )
+    return Result(completed.returncode, completed.stdout, completed.stderr)
+
+
+def make_fixture(base: Path) -> Path:
+    fixture = base / "fixture"
+    fixture.mkdir()
+    (fixture / "alpha.txt").write_bytes(b"a")
+    (fixture / "Beta.TXT").write_bytes(b"beta")
+    (fixture / "item2.log").write_bytes(b"22")
+    (fixture / "item10.log").write_bytes(b"ten bytes!")
+    (fixture / ".dotfile").write_bytes(b"dot")
+    (fixture / "_legacy").write_bytes(b"legacy")
+    (fixture / "space name").write_bytes(b"space")
+    sub = fixture / "subdir"
+    sub.mkdir()
+    (sub / "child.txt").write_bytes(b"child")
+    deep = sub / "nested"
+    deep.mkdir()
+    (deep / "leaf").write_bytes(b"leaf")
+
+    # Whole-second timestamps avoid filesystem precision differences between
+    # processes while still exercising all date-based sort directions.
+    epoch = 1_700_000_000
+    for index, path in enumerate(sorted(fixture.rglob("*"), key=str)):
+        stamp = epoch + index * 60
+        os.utime(path, (stamp, stamp), follow_symlinks=False)
+    return fixture
+
+
+def cases(path: Path, missing: Path) -> list[Case]:
+    common = ("--color=never", "--icons=never")
+    target = str(path)
+    return [
+        Case("version", ("--version",)),
+        Case("unknown-option", ("--not-an-eza-option",)),
+        Case("missing-path", (*common, str(missing))),
+        Case("lines", (*common, "--oneline", target)),
+        Case("all", (*common, "--oneline", "--all", target)),
+        Case("almost-all", (*common, "--oneline", "--almost-all", target)),
+        Case("reverse", (*common, "--oneline", "--reverse", target)),
+        Case("sort-name-sensitive", (*common, "--oneline", "--sort=Name", target)),
+        Case("sort-extension", (*common, "--oneline", "--sort=extension", target)),
+        Case("sort-size", (*common, "--oneline", "--sort=size", target)),
+        Case("sort-modified", (*common, "--oneline", "--sort=modified", target)),
+        Case("dirs-first", (*common, "--oneline", "--group-directories-first", target)),
+        Case("only-dirs", (*common, "--oneline", "--only-dirs", target)),
+        Case("only-files", (*common, "--oneline", "--only-files", target)),
+        Case("ignore-glob", (*common, "--oneline", "--ignore-glob=*.log", target)),
+        Case("classify", (*common, "--oneline", "--classify=always", target)),
+        Case("quotes", (*common, "--oneline", target)),
+        Case("no-quotes", (*common, "--oneline", "--no-quotes", target)),
+        Case("grid-narrow", (*common, "--grid", "--width=18", target)),
+        Case("grid-across", (*common, "--grid", "--across", "--width=32", target)),
+        Case("long", (*common, "--long", target)),
+        Case("long-bytes", (*common, "--long", "--bytes", target)),
+        Case("long-header", (*common, "--long", "--header", target)),
+        Case("long-no-fields", (*common, "--long", "--no-permissions", "--no-filesize", "--no-time", target)),
+        Case("long-created", (*common, "--long", "--created", "--time-style=long-iso", target)),
+        Case("tree", (*common, "--tree", target)),
+        Case("tree-level-one", (*common, "--tree", "--level=1", target)),
+        Case("tree-long", (*common, "--tree", "--long", "--no-time", target)),
+        Case("recurse", (*common, "--oneline", "--recurse", "--level=2", target)),
+        Case("stdin-path", (*common, "--oneline", "--stdin"), (target + "\n").encode()),
+    ]
+
+
+def escaped(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return repr(data.decode("utf-8", errors="backslashreplace"))
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--candidate",
+        nargs="+",
+        default=[sys.executable, str(ROOT / "eza_port.py")],
+        help="candidate command, before eza arguments",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--case", action="append", dest="selected")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    if not REFERENCE.is_file():
+        print(f"reference binary not found: {REFERENCE}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+    failures = 0
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="eza-port-", dir=ROOT / ".tura") as tmp:
+        temp = Path(tmp)
+        fixture = make_fixture(temp)
+        corpus = cases(fixture, temp / "missing")
+        if args.selected:
+            names = set(args.selected)
+            corpus = [case for case in corpus if case.name in names]
+
+        for case in corpus:
+            expected = run([str(REFERENCE)], case, ROOT)
+            actual = run(args.candidate, case, ROOT)
+            if actual == expected:
+                print(f"PASS {case.name}")
+                continue
+            failures += 1
+            print(f"FAIL {case.name}")
+            if actual.status != expected.status:
+                print(f"  status expected={expected.status} actual={actual.status}")
+            if actual.stdout != expected.stdout:
+                print(f"  stdout expected={escaped(expected.stdout)}")
+                print(f"  stdout actual  ={escaped(actual.stdout)}")
+            if actual.stderr != expected.stderr:
+                print(f"  stderr expected={escaped(expected.stderr)}")
+                print(f"  stderr actual  ={escaped(actual.stderr)}")
+
+    print(f"{len(corpus) - failures}/{len(corpus)} differential cases passed")
+    return 1 if failures else 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
*** End Patch
